name: Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma Data Center

profile.reading: This facility in south Durant, Oklahoma, sits on the headquarters campus of the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma, a federally recognized tribal nation and, by its own account, the third largest Indian nation in the United States, with more than 200,000 tribal members and more than 12,000 employees and associates. The Choctaw Nation traces its origins to a homeland in what is now Mississippi and Alabama, and its people were among the first Native nations forced west along the Trail of Tears in the 1830s. Today the nation's historic reservation spans roughly 10,864 square miles across eight whole counties and parts of five more in southeastern Oklahoma, an area comparable in size to the state of Maryland. The Choctaw Nation operates as a constitutional government with three branches. An elected Chief and Assistant Chief lead the executive branch, a twelve member Tribal Council elected from twelve districts serves as the legislature, and a separate tribal court system administers justice. The nation's main administrative offices sit on Chukka Hina in Durant, near the Texas border about eighty miles north of Dallas, and the campus houses the departments and service centers that run the tribe's government, health, education, housing, and economic development programs, alongside its gaming, hospitality, manufacturing, and other business operations. Running a tribal government and business enterprise of this scale requires substantial information technology infrastructure to manage member services, health records, financial systems, and internal communications, and this record reflects a computing facility located within or alongside the Choctaw Nation's Durant headquarters buildings supporting that infrastructure. No source reviewed for this entry published a specific power capacity, dedicated server room square footage, or equipment inventory for the facility distinct from the headquarters campus as a whole, and none is estimated here. This entry is filed as a genuine, government operated computing facility supporting a large and active tribal government's own operations, distinct from a commercial data center that leases space or capacity to outside customers. The Choctaw Nation's government also operates an extensive network of tribally owned businesses, including casinos and resorts, healthcare facilities, manufacturing operations, and other enterprises, and coordinating payroll, scheduling, member records, and financial systems across a workforce and business portfolio of that size is itself the kind of task that depends on centralized computing infrastructure. Durant, where the headquarters campus sits, is in Bryan County near the Texas state line, roughly eighty miles from the Dallas Fort Worth area, and the online services the tribe offers its members, including an internet portal for applying to programs with securely stored documentation, likewise depend on the kind of server and network infrastructure this record is documenting. A government and business operation with more than 200,000 members and 12,000 or more employees and associates represents genuine, substantial computing demand distinct from the token IT closet found in a small business.

reading.body:
This facility is attributed to the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma in Durant, Oklahoma, but its specifications are not published. The site's research was exhausted without confirming whether a dedicated data center exists at this location or finding any technical specifications, power capacity, or cooling capability. A tribal headquarters building opened there in 2018 alongside various government services and tribal enterprises including document archiving, but no sourcing confirmed a data center facility or its infrastructure.

Oklahoma has no published capacity figures from any data center operator on record with this site. Nine facilities are mapped in the state, but none report their power draw publicly. This location cannot be ranked against other sites in the state or region because the capacity is unknown.

Without published specifications, this campus cannot be assessed for relevance to AI scaling. The absence of a confirmed facility or stated power capacity means it does not yet appear in any measurable capacity analysis of the US AI infrastructure landscape.
